title: 3-Read Friday #81: Back to School Resources, AI in Schools, and Bookletising the Curriculum
author: Craig Barton
summary: 3-Read Friday #81 opens the new school year with Colleen Young's compilation of start-of-term maths resources spanning Reception to A Level, before turning to two more substantial picks. Carl Hendrick tackles AI's growing footprint in schools, arguing that curriculum planning needs disciplinary expertise to avoid AI-generated curricula that look convincing but lack real structure, that adaptive learning must go beyond mere difficulty adjustment to be genuinely responsive, and that human judgement must stay central to AI-assisted assessment. Jon Fant then describes his department's shift toward bookletising the maths curriculum, using a new calculation unit built around the area model and two-coloured counters to expand access to more advanced content. Barton's throughline for the issue is readiness for the year ahead, whether that means stocked resource shelves, a considered AI policy, or a coherently sequenced curriculum.
points: Colleen is one of the OG maths bloggers and is still going strong -- Barton frames her back-to-school compilation as a practical resource haul for the opening weeks of term.

I am fascinated by the impact AI is having, and will have, on our jobs and the education of our students -- Barton signals that Hendrick's three-part framework for school AI policy is his most substantial pick of the issue.

Booklets, PowerPoints and departmental approaches to topics have been regular themes in my newsletters and podcasts over the last few years, and always divide opinion -- Barton frames Fant's bookletising project as a continuation of an ongoing, contested debate about curriculum resourcing.
I loved reading Jon's endeavours to develop a coherent approach across his maths department to two key topics -- the emphasis is on department-wide coherence, not just one teacher's classroom.
